# Secure Low-Level Code

Memory-safety bugs dominate real-world agent failures. On SecureAgentBench (OSS-Fuzz C/C++ projects; [Chen et al., *SecureAgentBench*, arXiv:2509.22097](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.22097)), **over 80% of functionally correct agent patches for CWE-120 still contained the overflow**. Newly *introduced* bugs were mostly double free (CWE-415), use-after-free (CWE-416), compiler-removed buffer clearing (CWE-14), unchecked copies (CWE-120), and out-of-bounds reads. The rules below target exactly these.

## 0. Prefer a memory-safe option when you have the choice
For new components, prefer Rust, Go, or a managed language (see CISA/NSA, *The Case for Memory Safe Roadmaps*, 2023). In existing C/C++, use the safest local idioms: C++ containers, `std::span`, `std::string_view` with lifetime care, smart pointers. Don't rewrite unasked.

## 1. Bounds: every write and read has a proven size [CWE-120, 121, 122, 125, 787]
- **Banned**: `gets`, `strcpy`, `strcat`, `sprintf`, `vsprintf`, `scanf("%s")`, `strtok` (not reentrant), `alloca` with unbounded size. Avoid `strncpy` (no NUL guarantee) and `strncat` (confusing size).
- **Use**: `snprintf(dst, sizeof dst, ...)` and check its return (`ret < 0 || (size_t)ret >= sizeof dst` → truncated), `strlcpy`/`strlcat` where available, or `memcpy` **after** an explicit length check. Use `fgets` and `getline`.
- Always pass **(pointer, length)** pairs. Never let a callee guess the buffer size. Use `sizeof` on arrays, not on pointers.
- **Parsing untrusted input** (network packets, files): keep `pos` and `len`. Before *every* read, check `need <= len - pos`. That form avoids overflow, unlike `pos + need <= len`.
  ```c
  /* ✅ length-prefixed field reader */
  static int read_field(const uint8_t *buf, size_t len, size_t *pos, uint8_t *out, size_t out_cap, size_t *out_len) {
      if (len - *pos < 2) return -1;                       /* room for the length header? */
      size_t n = ((size_t)buf[*pos] << 8) | buf[*pos + 1];
      *pos += 2;
      if (n > len - *pos || n > out_cap) return -1;        /* claimed length must fit both input and output */
      memcpy(out, buf + *pos, n);
      *pos += n; *out_len = n;
      return 0;
  }
  ```
- Off-by-one: allocate `len + 1` for NUL-terminated strings. Loops use `i < n`, not `i <= n`.
- C++: `.at()` in non-hot paths. `std::array`/`std::vector` instead of raw arrays. `std::span` for views. No `operator[]` with unchecked external indices.

## 2. Integers [CWE-190, 191, 681, 194]
- Sizes are `size_t`. Never compare signed and unsigned. Reject negative lengths *before* converting.
- Check before multiplying for allocation: `if (n != 0 && size > SIZE_MAX / n) fail;`, or use `calloc(n, size)`, `reallocarray`, or `__builtin_mul_overflow` / `ckd_mul` (C23).
- Use `strtol`/`strtoul` with `errno = 0`, end-pointer, and range checks. Never `atoi`.
- Watch implicit truncation (`size_t` → `int`, `uint32_t` → `uint16_t`) on length fields.

## 3. Lifetime & ownership [CWE-415, 416, 401, 762, 825]
- **One owner per allocation.** Document who frees. Free in exactly one place. Set the pointer to `NULL` right after `free`.
- Use a single-exit cleanup pattern (`goto cleanup`) so every error path frees exactly once:
  ```c
  int process(const char *path) {
      int rc = -1; FILE *f = NULL; char *buf = NULL;
      if (!(f = fopen(path, "rb"))) goto cleanup;
      if (!(buf = malloc(BUF_SZ))) goto cleanup;
      /* ... */
      rc = 0;
  cleanup:
      free(buf);
      if (f) fclose(f);
      return rc;
  }
  ```
- Don't keep pointers into a buffer that may be `realloc`'d, or into a container that may grow (iterator/reference invalidation in C++).
- Never return pointers or references to stack locals. Watch `std::string_view`/`span` outliving their owner.
- C++: RAII everywhere (`std::unique_ptr`, `std::vector`, lock guards). No raw `new`/`delete`. Match `new[]`/`delete[]`. Rule of 0/3/5.
- After moving from an object (C++), don't use it except to reassign or destroy.

## 4. Initialization [CWE-457, 908, 665]
Initialize every variable at declaration (`= {0}`, `= {}`). Check `malloc` for NULL and zero it (`calloc`) if any field may be read before writing. Compile with `-ftrivial-auto-var-init=zero` where supported.

## 5. Format strings & variadics [CWE-134]
A format string is always a literal: `printf("%s", msg)`, `syslog(LOG_ERR, "%s", msg)`. Enable `-Wformat=2 -Werror=format-security`. Annotate wrappers with `__attribute__((format(printf, N, M)))`.

## 6. Secrets in memory [CWE-14, 226, 244]
- Wipe keys and passwords with `explicit_bzero` (glibc/BSD), `memset_s` (C11 Annex K), `SecureZeroMemory` (Windows), `sodium_memzero`, or `OPENSSL_cleanse`. Plain `memset` before `free` **is removed by the optimizer**.
- Compare MACs and tokens in constant time (`CRYPTO_memcmp`, `sodium_memcmp`). No `memcmp`/early-exit loops on secrets. Avoid secret-dependent branches and table indices in crypto code.
- Lock sensitive pages if needed (`mlock`) and avoid core dumps of secrets (`prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0)`).

## 7. Files, processes, races [CWE-367, 377, 78, 59]
- TOCTOU: don't `access()`/`stat()` and then `open()`. Open first, then `fstat` the fd. Use `O_NOFOLLOW`, `O_CLOEXEC`, `O_EXCL|O_CREAT` for new files, and `openat` relative to a trusted dir fd.
- Temp files: `mkstemp` / `tmpfile`, never `tmpnam`/`mktemp`.
- Processes: `posix_spawn`/`execve` with argv arrays. No `system()`/`popen()` with input. Drop privileges (`setgid` then `setuid`, check returns). Sanitize the environment.
- Threads: protect shared state with mutexes or atomics. Data races are UB.
- Signal handlers: only async-signal-safe functions.

## 8. Error handling [CWE-252, 253, 754]
Check every return value: `malloc`, `read`/`write` (short reads!), `snprintf`, `fclose`, `setuid`, `pthread_*`. Mark functions `[[nodiscard]]` / `__attribute__((warn_unused_result))`.

## 9. Build hardening (always add to new build files)
See [hardening-flags.md](securevibe/skills/secure-lowlevel/references/hardening-flags.md). Minimum for GCC/Clang:
```
-O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wformat=2 -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Werror=format-security -Werror=implicit
-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3 -D_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS -fstack-protector-strong -fstack-clash-protection
-fcf-protection=full (x86) / -mbranch-protection=standard (arm64) -fPIE -pie -Wl,-z,relro,-z,now -Wl,-z,noexecstack
```

## 10. Verify: sanitizers & fuzzing
For parsers and anything touching untrusted bytes, add a test build with `-fsanitize=address,undefined` and a libFuzzer/AFL++ harness. See [sanitizers-fuzzing.md](securevibe/skills/secure-lowlevel/references/sanitizers-fuzzing.md). If you can, compile and run the tests with ASan before replying.
